chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who breastfeeds a boy belonging to her from a female slave until she weans him; is it permissible for her to sell him? He said, 'There is no prohibition upon her regarding its price. Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) not say, "What is prohibited by lineage is also prohibited by breastfeeding"? Did he not become her son?' I went to write it down, so he said, 'And something like this is not written down.'
ai.seo_question: Can a woman sell a slave child she breastfed, and what is the basis in hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while breastfeeding establishes a kinship bond (radāʿ) making the child akin to a son, this specific case of a slave child does not create the same prohibitions as biological lineage, thus permitting the mother to sell him. He cites the Prophet’s general principle that 'what is prohibited by lineage is prohibited by breastfeeding,' but distinguishes this ruling from formal legal codification, noting it is not typically recorded in written collections. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between established legal precedents and specific contextual rulings that remain uncodified.
